title: Porphyry copper deposits (all subtypes)
percentile_convention: USGS: p90 is the value that 90% of deposits equal or exceed (the small end); p10 the large end

sources.citation: Singer, D.A., Berger, V.I., and Moring, B.C., 2008, Porphyry copper deposits of the world: database and grade and tonnage models, 2008: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2008-1155, 45 p.
Singer, D.A., Berger, V.I., and Moring, B.C., 2008, companion data file PorCuTX2008.txt (tab-delimited porphyry copper database, 690 records) of U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2008-1155.

John, D.A., Ayuso, R.A., Barton, M.D., Blakely, R.J., Bodnar, R.J., Dilles, J.H., Gray, Floyd, Graybeal, F.T., Mars, J.C., McPhee, D.K., Seal, R.R., Taylor, R.D., and Vikre, P.G., 2010, Porphyry copper deposit model, chap. B of Mineral deposit models for resource assessment: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2010-5070-B, 169 p.
Not a publication. Marks a value supplied by the digitiser because the engine needs a number and no USGS source opened for this file states one; the entry's note says what the value is based on.

Singer, D.A., Berger, V.I., Menzie, W.D., and Berger, B.R., 2005, Porphyry copper deposit density: Economic Geology, v. 100, no. 3, p. 491-514, doi:10.2113/gsecongeo.100.3.491. Abstract as published on the USGS Publications Warehouse (record 70197200; all four authors USGS).
sources.licence: Abstract text on a USGS (public-domain) web page; the full article is published by the Society of Economic Geologists. Only facts (numbers) are taken from it.

tonnage_mt.where: Table 1 ('General Cu, Tons'), PDF p. 9; same values printed as intercepts on Fig. 2 ('Tonnage model for all porphyry copper deposits'), PDF p. 15. The report has no printed page numbers.
tonnage_mt.note: Tonnage in millions of metric tons of ore, 'based on the total production, reserves, and resources at the lowest possible cutoff grade' (PDF p. 5). Only well-explored deposits with a value in the Tonnage field are in the model (PDF p. 7-8). Supergene ore is inside the model: 'Deposits that may be derived from, or affected by, hypogene and supergene processes are included in the models' (PDF p. 4). Figure 7 is NOT the all-deposit model: it is the Cu-Au subtype (34/200/1,200 Mt, PDF p. 20).

cu_pct.where: Table 1 ('General Cu, Cu grade'), PDF p. 9; same intercepts printed on Fig. 3, PDF p. 16
cu_pct.note: p10 is 0.75 % (Table 1 and the Fig. 3 label), not 0.80 %: 0.80 is only an axis tick on Fig. 3. Every deposit reports Cu.

mo_pct.where: Table 1 ('General Cu, Mo grade'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 4, PDF p. 17
mo_pct.note: Percentiles include deposits with no reported Mo, which the report treats as zero ('Grades not available (always for by-products) are treated as zero', PDF p. 5; 'Percentiles of grades that contain unreported values, such as Mo, Ag, and Au, were based on the observed distributions', PDF p. 8). Fig. 4 prints the p50 intercept as 0.0023 (Table 1 rounds it to 0.002). n_reported = 228 of 422 (0.540) is counted from the companion data file PorCuTX2008.txt (source ofr2008-1155-data: records with Tonnage > 0 and Molybdenum grade > 0); it agrees with the top of the Fig. 4 curve at ~0.54 (digitised).

au_gpt.where: Table 1 ('General Cu, Au grade'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 5, PDF p. 18; n = 256 stated in text, PDF p. 8
au_gpt.note: Percentiles include deposits with no reported Au, treated as zero (PDF p. 5, p. 8). n_reported = 256 of 422 (0.607): the text gives n = 256 for the tonnage-Au correlation, the companion data file has 256 records with Au > 0, and the Fig. 5 curve starts at ~0.61 (digitised).

ag_gpt.where: Table 1 ('General Cu, Ag grade'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 6, PDF p. 19 (only the p10 intercept, 3.8, is labelled)
ag_gpt.note: Percentiles include deposits with no reported Ag, treated as zero (PDF p. 5, p. 8); fewer than half the deposits report Ag, so p90 and p50 are 0.0 (as printed in Table 1). n_reported = 172 of 422 (0.408) counted from the companion data file PorCuTX2008.txt (source ofr2008-1155-data); agrees with the top of the Fig. 6 curve at ~0.41 (digitised).

correlations.where: Text, PDF p. 8 ('shows a low positive correlation (r = 0.1) that is not significant at the one percent level'); Fig. 1 label 'r = 0.1*', PDF p. 14
correlations.note: Significant at the 5 % level only (the report's '*' convention, PDF p. 8), not at 1 %. Recomputing Pearson r on log10 values from the companion data file gives 0.100 (n 422), so the coefficients are correlations of logarithms.

correlations.where: Text, PDF p. 8 ('Tonnage is correlated with gold grade (r = -0.28**, n = 256)')
correlations.note: Significant at the 1 % level (**). n = deposits that report Au (zeros excluded). The companion data file reproduces r = -0.283 on log10 values.

correlations.where: Text, PDF p. 8 ('gold is correlated with molybdenum (r = -0.16*, n = 148)')
correlations.note: Significant at the 5 % level (*). n = deposits reporting both Mo and Au. The companion data file reproduces r = -0.165 on log10 values.

Significant at the 1 % level (**). The report does not print n; 148 is the number of deposits reporting both Au and Ag in the companion data file (source ofr2008-1155-data), on which log10 values give r = 0.256.

ore_density_t_m3.where: not stated in ofr2008-1155 (whole report and data-file field list read) or sir2010-5070-B (searched for density, specific gravity, t/m3, g/cm3); also absent from SIR 2010-5090-H, SIR 2018-5160, OFR 01-218 and TM 7-C23
ore_density_t_m3.note: PLACEHOLDER, NOT FROM USGS. The engine's Sizing.ore_density_t_m3 is a required number, so a value is supplied: 2.7 t/m3 is a generic density for fresh intermediate-to-felsic intrusive rock (granodiorite / quartz monzonite, roughly 2.6-2.8 t/m3) from general geological knowledge. USGS tonnages are in metric tons, so volume = tonnage / density. SIR 2010-5070-B p. 4 (PDF p. 18) says only, qualitatively, that hypogene and supergene gangue minerals 'have lower densities than the primary rock-forming minerals ... they replace'.

deposits_per_1e5_km2.where: USGS Publications Warehouse record 70197200, abstract, third paragraph ('Ninety percent of the control areas have densities of four or more deposits, 50 percent have densities of 15 or more deposits, and 10 percent have densities of 35 or more deposits per 100,000 km2')
deposits_per_1e5_km2.note: Densities of deposits AND prospects (286 counted, more than half uncovered) per 100,000 km2 of EXPOSED permissive rock in 19 well-explored control areas; range 2 to 128. Density is inversely related to the exposed permissive area, and the authors provide a regression for number of deposits against area (coefficients not in the abstract). Deposits combined under the same 2-km rule. No USGS numbered report restating the 4/15/35 figures was found; SIR 2010-5090-C compares tract densities with this model but does not reprint the percentiles.

min_separation_m.where: 'Rules applied', PDF p. 4 ('All mineralized rock or alteration within two (2) kilometers was combined into one deposit'); restated in sir2010-5070-B p. 25 (PDF p. 39) and in the usgs-pw-70197200 abstract
min_separation_m.note: The rule combines deposits whose alteration zones are within 2 km of each other (e.g. El Pachon and Los Pelambres are one record). The field 'Includes' names the combined deposits.

subtype_20c_tonnage_mt.where: Table 1 ('Cu-Au (20c) Tons'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 7, PDF p. 20
subtype_20c_tonnage_mt.note: Porphyry Cu-Au subtype (model 20c: Au/Mo >= 30 with Au in g/t and Mo in %; or no Mo reported and Au > 0.2 g/t; PDF p. 6). value = p50.

subtype_20c_cu_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 8, PDF p. 21

subtype_20c_mo_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 9, PDF p. 22 (prints the p10 intercept as 0.0065)
subtype_20c_mo_pct.note: value = p50. Includes zeros for unreported Mo. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_20c_ag_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 11, PDF p. 24
subtype_20c_ag_gpt.note: value = p50. Includes zeros for unreported Ag. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_20c_au_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 10, PDF p. 23
subtype_20c_au_gpt.note: value = p50. All Cu-Au deposits report Au (by definition).

subtype_17_tonnage_mt.where: Table 1 ('Cu (17) Tons'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 12, PDF p. 25
subtype_17_tonnage_mt.note: Porphyry Cu subtype (model 17: 3 < Au/Mo < 30). value = p50.

subtype_17_cu_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 13, PDF p. 26

subtype_17_mo_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 14, PDF p. 27
subtype_17_mo_pct.note: value = p50. Includes zeros for unreported Mo. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_17_ag_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 16, PDF p. 29
subtype_17_ag_gpt.note: value = p50. Includes zeros. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_17_au_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 15, PDF p. 28
subtype_17_au_gpt.note: value = p50. Includes zeros. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_21a_tonnage_mt.where: Table 1 ('Cu-Mo (21a) Tons'), PDF p. 9; Fig. 17, PDF p. 30
subtype_21a_tonnage_mt.note: Porphyry Cu-Mo subtype (model 21a: Au/Mo <= 3; or no Au reported and Mo > 0.03 %). Tonnages significantly larger than the other two subtypes (p = 0.004, PDF p. 8-9). value = p50. CAUTION: the p10 arrow on Fig. 17 lands at about 3,800 Mt on the axis (digitised, +/- 300 Mt) although both the label and Table 1 print 4,800; the companion data file gives an empirical p10 (the tonnage exceeded by 10 % of the 51 deposits) near 3,100 Mt. 4,800 may be a typo for 3,800; the printed value is kept.

subtype_21a_cu_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 18, PDF p. 31

subtype_21a_mo_pct.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 19, PDF p. 32

subtype_21a_ag_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 21, PDF p. 34
subtype_21a_ag_gpt.note: value = p50. Includes zeros. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_21a_au_gpt.where: Table 1, PDF p. 9; Fig. 20, PDF p. 33
subtype_21a_au_gpt.note: value = p50. Includes zeros. n_reported counted from the companion data file (ofr2008-1155-data).

subtype_21a_r_tonnage_mo.where: Text, PDF p. 9 ('Molybdenum grades are inversely related to tonnages in the Cu-Mo subtype (r = -0.40**. N = 51)')
subtype_21a_r_tonnage_mo.note: Cu-Mo subtype only; significant at the 1 % level. The companion data file reproduces r = -0.403 on log10 values.

subtype_rule_au_mo_ratio_cu_au_min.where: 'Types of porphyry copper deposits', PDF p. 6
subtype_rule_au_mo_ratio_cu_au_min.note: Cu-Au (20c) if Au/Mo >= 30; Cu-Mo (21a) if Au/Mo <= 3; Cu (17) otherwise (after Cox and Singer, 1992). With no Mo reported, Au > 0.2 g/t gives Cu-Au; with no Au reported, Mo > 0.03 % gives Cu-Mo.

subtype_rule_au_mo_ratio_cu_mo_max.where: 'Types of porphyry copper deposits', PDF p. 6

ore_area_km2.where: Table E1, p. 28 (PDF p. 42); text p. 25 (PDF p. 39)
ore_area_km2.note: Area of ore projected to the surface, from the Singer and others (2008) compilation, mostly computed as ellipses (pi*a*b/4); includes deposits without tonnage. value = median. Chuquicamata has the largest ore area.

sulfide_area_km2.where: Table E1, p. 28 (PDF p. 42); text p. 25 (PDF p. 39)
sulfide_area_km2.note: Area of sulfide-bearing (pyrite) rock projected to the surface. value = median.

alteration_area_km2.where: Table E1, p. 28 (PDF p. 42); text p. 25 (PDF p. 39)
alteration_area_km2.note: Area of hydrothermally altered rock projected to the surface. value = median. Ray (82 km2) and Escondida (78 km2) are the largest.

sulfide_area_vs_cu_content_r.note: Area of sulfide system (km2) versus contained Cu; significant at 1 %. n is not printed; the companion data file has 137 deposits with both a sulfide area and a tonnage.

sulfide_area_vs_cu_content_intercept.where: Fig. 26 label 'log Cu = 5.67 + 0.796 log sulfide area', PDF p. 39
sulfide_area_vs_cu_content_intercept.note: Regression printed on the figure: log10(Cu, metric tons) = 5.67 + 0.796 log10(sulfide area, km2). The y axis is in millions of tons, and the line passes ~0.47 Mt Cu at 1 km2, so Cu in the equation is in metric tons.

sulfide_area_vs_cu_content_slope.unit: log10 t Cu per log10 km2

emplacement_depth_km_median_20c.note: Median line of the Cu-Au box read on the log axis as 1.18 km (+/- 0.03). The companion data file gives a median of 1.15 km over 16 deposits with tonnage (whiskers 0.2-2.53 km match the figure). Cu-Au deposits formed significantly shallower than Cu-Mo (p < 0.001, PDF p. 10).

emplacement_depth_km_median_17.note: Read as 1.52 km (+/- 0.04); data file median 1.5 km over 19 deposits (whiskers 0.6-4.6 km).

emplacement_depth_km_median_21a.note: Read as 2.33 km (+/- 0.06); data file median 2.3 km over 12 deposits (range 1.3-4.8 km).

hypogene_ore_vertical_extent_km_max_typi.note: 'The vertical extent of hypogene copper ore in porphyry copper deposits is generally 1 to 1.5 km or less'; mineralized rock can continue several km deeper. Hydrothermal effects may extend 10 km or more outward and to 10 km below the paleosurface (same page).

assoc_placer_au_within_10km_pct_20c.where: Fig. 23 bar chart ('placer Au', Porphyry Cu-Au bar), PDF p. 36
assoc_placer_au_within_10km_pct_20c.note: Percent of porphyry Cu-Au deposits with a placer Au deposit within 10 km; read +/- 0.3 points. Text (PDF p. 10): 'Placer gold deposits are more common near gold-rich porphyry copper deposits.' Not reproducible from the 2008 data file's 'Assoc Deposits less 10km' field (which gives 4 of 55 Cu-Au records that have association data, 7 %), so the figure's denominator is unknown.

deposit_density_range_max.note: Highest control-area density; the histogram is skewed to high values.

unreported_correlations.where: not printed in ofr2008-1155; computed from PorCuTX2008.txt
unreported_correlations.note: OFR 2008-1155 prints no coefficient for tonnage-Mo, tonnage-Ag, Cu-Mo, Cu-Au, Cu-Ag or Mo-Ag. For reference only (OUR computation, not a USGS-published number; the same computation reproduces all five printed coefficients to two decimals): Pearson r of log10 values over deposits reporting both, tonnage-Mo -0.055 (n 228), tonnage-Ag -0.076 (n 172), Cu-Mo -0.057 (n 228), Cu-Au -0.005 (n 256), Cu-Ag 0.042 (n 172), Mo-Ag 0.096 (n 127).
